description:
Position every event append at the end of the log's last newline-terminated line, so an unterminated final line is an uncommitted append that the next append overwrites instead of a fragment it buries.

## Background

The finalizer appends at the captured log length and, when the log ends in an unterminated final line, prefixes a separator newline (`compose_events`, `crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:615-630`; offset at `:1241`; `captured_log_end` at `:639`). That turns the fragment into a permanent malformed middle line. To avoid corrupting the log, the finalizer refuses every append over an unterminated, unparseable final line unless the mutation writes a profile marker (`:1195-1206`, `MutationError::UncertifiedTornTail`). `finalize_audit_append` (`:1258`) shares the same path. Both backends already apply an event append at its offset and truncate to the offset plus its bytes (`storage/redo_apply.rs:302-320`, `storage/memory.rs:692-712`; the overlay at `repository_state/overlay.rs:120-126`), and the end-of-log probe already holds the final line (owner decision @/issue/c88822a5/decision/D-1). Tests pinning today's behaviour: `mutation.rs:1772-1810,2449-2560` and `commands/profile.rs:5219-5240,6365-6395`. The rustdoc and test prose of the functions this changes go with them (`@/inv/essential-code-prose`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The length a mutation reads from the event log is its committed length: the end of its last newline-terminated line, which the end-of-log probe determines. Every event append, `finalize_audit_append` included, is positioned at that length and writes no separator newline. The rustdoc of `compose_events` and `captured_log_end` (`mutation.rs:617,632`), the offset test's doc (`:1769`) and its assertion message (`:2485`) say committed length.
- [hard] REQ-02: No mutation refuses to append over an unterminated final line, and a finalizer unit test shows that an append over one starts at that line's offset and leaves a log every line of which is newline-terminated.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Event appends land at the log's committed length
